sources.entry: typer - Modern CLI framework that uses Python type hints. Built on Click.

summary.one_liner: Typer is a Python library for building CLI applications from standard type hints, with a companion `typer` command that can run ordinary scripts as CLIs.
summary.what_it_does: Typer turns Python function parameters and their type annotations into CLI arguments and options, so the same declaration drives parsing, validation, and help text. It supports single-command scripts via typer.run(), and multi-command apps built with typer.Typer() and @app.command() decorators, including nested groups of subcommands. Boolean parameters automatically become --flag/--no-flag pairs. The README says it provides automatic --help and shell auto-completion for Bash, Zsh, Fish, and PowerShell. A `typer` command can run a script such as main.py directly as a CLI, even if the script does not import Typer. Typer's README describes it as built on type hints and as FastAPI's sibling for CLIs.
use_cases: building a command line tool in Python
adding subcommands to a Python script
turning a function into a CLI with options and arguments
running an existing Python script as a command line program
adding shell tab-completion to a Python CLI
how_to_run: python main.py Camila (after adding typer.run(main) to the script)
notable: Uses standard Python type hints as the only declaration syntax, with no new DSL
The `typer` command can run scripts that do not use Typer internally
Click source is vendored into Typer rather than installed as a dependency since 0.26.0
Boolean options automatically get --flag and --no-flag forms
caveats: typer-slim is no longer supported; since 0.22.0 it installs the full Typer package
Some Click functionality may stop being available as the vendored code diverges
Shell auto-completion works best when the app is packaged and installed or run via the typer command, per the README
keywords: auto completion bash zsh fish powershell
make my python script a cli
